blurb: Richard Hannay is on the run across Scotland with a dead man’s notebook full of secrets.
source: The Thirty-Nine Steps by John Buchan (1915). Read it in your own copy, or borrow it free from your library.

streets.name: The Man Who Died
streets.blurb: A frightened neighbour, Scudder, hides in Hannay’s flat — and leaves behind a little notebook in code.
streets.how: Look round the flat for clues, then crack the code on Scudder’s notebook lock.

clues.label: The chessboard
clues.text: Every night Scudder and Hannay played chess. Scudder liked puzzles: the first number is the number of pieces left on the board — 7.

clues.label: The clock
clues.text: The clock has stopped. Its hands point to 3.

clues.label: The window
clues.text: Scudder kept watching the street from here. On the glass he has drawn a little figure 9.

solve.label: The notebook lock
solve.prompt: Chessboard, clock, window — in that order.

streets.name: The Milkman
streets.blurb: Hannay must slip out of his flat past the men watching it.
streets.how: Dressed as the milkman, get past the watchers to the street corner. Hide behind the walls and in the doorways.

params.objective: Get past the watchers to the corner

streets.name: The Literary Innkeeper
streets.blurb: Off the train and onto the Galloway moors, with a monoplane searching the sky.
streets.how: Run across the moor — leap the burns and dodge the rocks before the aeroplane spots you.

params.objective: Cross the moor before you’re spotted

streets.name: The Radical Candidate
streets.blurb: Hannay is pushed onto a platform to make a speech at a meeting — with no warning at all.
streets.how: Keep to the rhythm of the speech: hit each word as it reaches the line.

params.done: Loud cheers! Nobody guessed you were on the run.

streets.name: The Spectacled Roadman
streets.blurb: Hannay swaps places with a roadman — spectacles, hat, pipe and all.
streets.how: In your roadman’s disguise, walk past the searchers to the end of the road. Duck behind the stone heaps if they look your way.

streets.name: The Bald Archaeologist
streets.blurb: Captured and locked in a dark storeroom. There must be a way out.
streets.how: Feel your way round the storeroom for clues, then work out how to get out.

params.objective: Find a way out of the storeroom

clues.label: The shutters
clues.text: The windows are heavily shuttered. A thin line of light shows round one of them.

clues.label: The boxes
clues.text: Old boxes and tins, smelling of chemicals. Best left well alone.

clues.label: A tool box
clues.text: Rusty tools — and an old screwdriver.

solve.label: The way out
solve.prompt: How can Hannay get out safely?
options: Use the screwdriver on the shutter by the line of light
Wait for the bald man to come back
solve.hint: Where is the light getting in?

params.done: Out through the shutter and away up the hillside!

streets.name: The Dry-Fly Fisherman
streets.blurb: Hannay must reach Sir Walter Bullivant in London — and make him believe the story.
streets.how: Run for it! Get to the end of the road before the Black Stone catches up.

skyRun.name: Out of Sight of the Aeroplane
skyRun.blurb: the rocky high points of the moor, with an aeroplane searching overhead.
skyRun.how: Leap between the high rocks to the top. Some rocks wobble — wait for them!

npcs.name: Richard Hannay
npcs.idle: I’ve been on the run for weeks. Never a dull moment.
npcs.thanks: Every page! Now I can read the whole notebook.

steps.text: Talk to Richard Hannay outside the district.
steps.say: Scudder’s little notebook came apart in the rain, and five pages have blown away. They’re in code — I need every one.

steps.text: Find the five pages of Scudder’s notebook.
Give the pages back to Hannay.
steps.say: Thirty-nine steps… high tide… It’s all here. Thank you!

vault.name: The House with the Steps
vault.blurb: an escape room about the whole chase: find the house with the thirty-nine steps and name the spies.
vault.intro: Sir Walter’s map room. The answer to Scudder’s riddle is somewhere on the coast tonight, at high tide. Open three locks to find the house and the spies.

stations.label: Hannay’s disguises
stations.text: Match each of Hannay’s disguises or tricks to where he used it.
stations.lesson: Hannay kept one step ahead by becoming whoever the moment needed.

solve.hint: Think about the order of the chase.

stations.label: The coast map
stations.text: High tide at 10.17 p.m. A villa on the cliff top, with a private staircase down to the beach. Hannay counts the steps: thirty-nine.
stations.lesson: Scudder’s riddle pointed to one house on the cliffs: the one with thirty-nine steps down to the sea.

solve.prompt: Which house has the thirty-nine steps?
options: Trafalgar Lodge, the villa on the cliff above the beach
solve.hint: Steps down to a private beach, where high tide matters.

stations.label: The window on the lawn
stations.text: Three ordinary-looking gentlemen are playing tennis. But the old one has a way of hooding his eyes, just like the bald archaeologist on the moor.
stations.lesson: The Black Stone looked like ordinary English gentlemen — that was their disguise.

solve.prompt: Are these men really harmless neighbours?
options: No — the old man’s hooded eyes give him away: they are the Black Stone
Yes — nobody playing tennis could be a spy
solve.hint: Who else had a way of hooding his eyes?

quiz.label: Sir Walter’s desk
quiz.lesson: You followed Hannay from his flat in London all the way to the steps by the sea.

vault.openText: The tide turns at 10.17 — and the door swings open.
vault.outro: The spies are caught at the top of the thirty-nine steps.
